newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rebounds after Mahathir's comments.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rebounds after Mahathir's comments.

text.p: The ringgit rebounded against the dollar as funds liquidated long dollar positions after Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad warned about possible action against currency speculators, dealers said.
Mahathir said on Monday the government would consider taking punitive actions against speculators. However, he did not outline what specific measures Malaysia might take.
"Dollar/ringgit plunged from 2.6500 to 2.6310 within half an hour of the news hitting the market," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6270/90 to a dollar.
Dealers said the ringgit's rise was aided by thin trading ahead of the month-end.
Currency movements were exaggerated by wide spreads of 30 to 50 points, they said.
Dealers said the market remains wary of possible capital controls in the face of recent barrage of criticism hurled at speculators by Malaysian officials.
Nervous operators were seen unloading dollars as many were uncertain of what the Malaysian government had up its sleeve, said dealers.
"The government has got some ideas on what to do but obviously we cannot just publish what we want to do...," Mahathir told reporters.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit to be supported at 2.6200. There was talk that Bank Negara Malaysia was checking rates around 2.6510/20 this morning.
